title: Trace Retention and Privacy
summary: Work through Trace Retention and Privacy.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Trace Retention and Privacy**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Operating Agents, § Trace Retention and Privacy
blocks.md: If a delayed regression suite for the trial that produced `ws_r19` fails hours after execution concludes, that trial suddenly becomes diagnostically indispensable. By that time, however, its runtime process has terminated and its model and tool spans have closed. The forensic value of the run depends entirely on what the telemetry system chose to keep. Trace retention therefore requires integration with final task verdicts and their arrival timelines, rather than relying purely on process exit codes or span completion markers.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Accounting records and head sampling
- Tail sampling and verdict windows
- Disclosure minimization
- Replay fidelity after redaction

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Trace retention matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Sampling may thin diagnostic detail but never the accounting record of admitted trials, verdicts, spend, and drops, and retention is chosen per verdict under storage and privacy budgets.

questions.q: The section **Trace Retention and Privacy** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Sampling may thin diagnostic detail but never the accounting record of admitted trials, verdicts, spend, and drops, and retention is chosen per verdict under storage and privacy budgets.
A release decision is a declared conjunctive rule written before data and applied to an evidence record that keeps verdicts, paired cohorts, and diagnostics.
Release exposure is staged so each stage answers its own question (offline gate, shadow execution, bounded canary), with sequential monitoring and hard tripwires that stop admission.
Release is justified by a scoped, inspectable safety case of claim, argument, evidence, assumptions, and residual uncertainty, and evidence for one claim does not establish the others.
